info.title: SWARA AI
info.description:
SWARA AI empowers Indian Kirana stores with multilingual voice ordering, intelligent product recognition, real-time inventory management, automated order processing, and actionable business insights.

Speech in and out is provided by Gnani AI Prisma (STT) and Timbre (TTS).

post.description: Always answers the same way, so it cannot be used to find out who has an account.

get.description:
What the web app asks on every page load. Unlike /me it answers 200 for a visitor, so a signed-out landing page
does not fill the browser console with 401 errors.

post.description:
Razorpay calls this with a signed event. The signature is checked over the exact bytes received before anything is read. Answers 200 for an event it
has already handled (so Razorpay stops retrying), 400 for a bad signature.

Spoken version of an assistant reply that is already stored.

The text is the one the server saved for that turn; nothing the caller sends is spoken, so this cannot be used to have arbitrary text read out
on the shop's Gnani credits. Repeating the call is free (same reply, same voice: served from the audio cache).

The browser reports how long the person waited. Shown in the owner's diagnostics next to the server's own stage times, and labelled as
browser-reported there.

Button fallback for 'confirm': goes through the same dialogue path as speech, and means "that's all, confirm".

A bare "confirm" typed while the assistant is asking "Anything else?" would be read as a yes to that question, so the
bill would not be saved and the shopkeeper would have to press the button twice. When that question is open, the button
first answers it ("that's all") to reach the read-back, then confirms. The button says nothing about the customer's
language, so it never changes the conversation language or the language stored on the order.
Set or add a quantity on the open bill without going through speech (same stock rules as a spoken order).

get.description: Paginated inventory for the Inventory screen (the plain /products list is kept for compatibility).
Stock as CSV, filtered like the Inventory screen. Declared before /products/{id}-style routes so the path is never read as an id.
Orders as CSV, one row per bill line, for the same filters the Orders screen uses. Declared before /orders/{order_id}.
Which ways of paying are available right now. Owners also see whether the secrets are set (never their values) and the webhook address.
Payments, newest first. ``since`` and ``until`` are India dates (inclusive). The counts per status honour every filter except status.
Owner only. Every figure is summed from the payments and refunds tables; a period with no payments shows zero.

post.description:
Start a payment for the order's server-side total. Sending the same ``idempotency_key`` again, or asking again while a payment of the same kind
is still open, returns that payment (HTTP 200) instead of starting a second one.
A person confirms a manual UPI payment after checking their bank or UPI app. It stays labelled as not verified by a payment provider.

The browser reports what Checkout returned. This does not trust it: the signature is checked with the key secret and Razorpay is then asked about the
payment before anything is marked paid.
Ask Razorpay where a waiting payment stands. A shop whose computer cannot receive webhooks finds out this way.

Owner only. A Razorpay payment is refunded through Razorpay and stays 'waiting' until Razorpay confirms; a cash or manual UPI payment is recorded as
refunded by the owner and labelled as not confirmed by a provider. Leave ``amount_paise`` out to refund what is left.

get.description: The invoice for an order. The first time it is opened it is given the next number; after that it always returns the same one.

Customers as CSV. Owner only: staff can open one customer at a time, but a bulk file of names and phone numbers is the owner's to take.
Declared before /{customer_id} so the path is never read as an id.
Where the catalogue came from, read from data/sources/MANIFEST.json (written by the fetch script).
Command-bar search across products, customers, orders and the reference catalogue.

post.description:
Real round trip: Timbre speaks a short phrase, Prisma transcribes that audio. Costs 2 calls.

``language`` picks which language to check (default English). It is a *loopback*: Prisma hears Timbre's synthetic voice, so a pass
shows that both services accept the language and the voice, not how well Prisma recognises a person speaking it.

get.description: Where the time goes for spoken orders (from the turns this server recorded) and how the Gnani calls are doing. Owner only.
